feedback: If you named a reflection: ask 'does the shape read the same way round, or the mirror way round?' Only reflection reverses sense — re-decide from that check.

If you gave only the angle: a rotation needs three things — centre, size, direction. Add each and test by reproducing the image (tracing paper pinned at the centre lets you turn to the stated angle and direction and verify congruence).
If the image lands in the wrong place: check whether the centre is correct; if it turns the wrong way, check the direction.
Mark a rotation description as incomplete until centre, angle AND direction are all present.
activities.intendedInsight: Checking sense is what distinguishes a rotation from a reflection, and a rotation is only fully specified by centre, size AND direction together. The centre and the angle always affect where the image lands. The direction matters for 90° turns, but a 180° turn lands in the same place either way.
learnerActions: On a grid showing a shape and its image already placed (produced by a rotation), work out which single transformation maps the first onto the second and reproduce it by setting the parameters yourself.
First try a reflection: flip the shape and compare handedness to the target — notice the 'sense' no longer matches (the target reads the same way round), so it cannot be a reflection.
Switch to rotation: choose a centre of rotation, set the angle of turn, and choose the direction (clockwise/anticlockwise) until your image lands exactly on the target.

State the full description aloud or in writing, e.g. 'rotation, 90° clockwise, about (2,1)', and check what each part controls: turning the same amount about a different centre makes the shape land somewhere else, and for a 90° turn, going the opposite direction lands it in a different place. (For a 180° turn, clockwise and anticlockwise give the same image, but still state the direction to keep the description complete.)
Confirm the image is congruent to the original (e.g. by tracing or matching vertices).
activities.title: Name it: reconstruct the transformation that produced the image

feedback: If the image sits level with the object rather than square across a sloping mirror: your joining lines are not perpendicular to the mirror. Draw the perpendicular from each vertex and step the equal distance beyond.
Avoid 'straight across' language so the idea survives sloping mirror lines.
If sense is not reversed, you have not reflected — check the handedness of the image against the original.
activities.intendedInsight: A reflection moves every point perpendicular to the mirror by an equal distance on the other side, so the mirror is the perpendicular bisector of each joining segment — this holds for sloping mirrors, not just level ones.
learnerActions: Given a shape and a mirror line (including sloping or offset lines, not just horizontal/vertical), draw the reflected image.
For each vertex, draw the perpendicular from the vertex to the mirror line and step an equal distance beyond it to place the image vertex.
Check that the mirror line is the perpendicular bisector of each segment joining a vertex to its image, and that the sense (handedness) of the shape is reversed.
Describe what you did as 'a reflection in [this] mirror line' and confirm the image is congruent to the original.
Repeat with a sloping mirror to make sure your method does not rely on 'straight across/down'.
activities.title: Produce a reflection in a sloping mirror line

feedback: If a landed vertex is reported as (up, across): re-anchor with 'across the corridor, then up the stairs' and re-check one labelled vertex together.
If only some vertices moved the right amount, remember the same displacement applies to every vertex.
activities.intendedInsight: A translation slides every point by the same displacement, preserving orientation, sense and size; coordinates are read across first, then up.
learnerActions: Translate a shape by a given displacement (e.g. 3 right and 2 up), applying the same movement to every vertex.
Describe the movement both as a vector and in left/right/up/down words.
Label the coordinates of the translated vertices, writing each as (across, up).
Check that orientation and sense are unchanged and that the image is congruent to the original.
activities.title: Translate by a vector and label coordinates carefully

feedback: Score a rotation description as correct only if centre, angle AND direction are all present.
For the rotation-vs-reflection item, point to sense: if handedness flipped it is a reflection, if sense is unchanged it is a rotation.
activities.intendedInsight: Describing a transformation precisely means using the correct defining marks — and a rotation description counts only when centre, angle and direction are all given.
learnerActions: Answer 'which transformation maps A to B?' where one distractor shows the same shape reflected (sense reversed) rather than rotated.
Fill in the three parts of a rotation description (centre, size, direction) for a shown image.
Draw the path/image to produce a reflection in a given mirror line.
activities.title: Precision check: discrete items for describing transformations
